I see plainly, sirs, whoever you may be, that Heaven, whose care it is to succor the
good, and even the wicked very often, here, in this remote spot, cut off from human intercourse,
sends me, though I deserve it not, those who seek to draw me away from this to some better
retreat, showing me by many and forcible arguments how unreasonably I act in leading
the life I do. But as they know, that if I escape from this evil I shall fall into another
still greater, perhaps they will set me down as a weak-minded man, or, what is worse, one
devoid of reason? Nor would it be any wonder, for I myself can perceive that the effect
of the recollection of my misfortunes is so great and works so powerfully to my ruin,
that in spite of myself I become at times like a stone, without feeling or consciousness.
And I come to feel the truth of it when they tell me, and show me proofs of the things
I have done when the terrible fit overmasters me, and all I can do is bewail my lot in vain,
and idly curse my destiny, and plead for my madness by telling how it was caused, to any
that care to hear it, for no reasonable beings on learning the cause will wonder at the effects,
and if they cannot help me at least, they will not blame me, and the repugnance they
feel at my wild ways will turn into pity for my woes.
